topic.angle: Why trade helps even a country that is better at everything

card.title: Better at everything, and still trading

panels.text: In 1817 David Ricardo pictured two countries, Portugal and England, each making cloth and wine of identical quality.
Portugal is better at both. One unit takes it 90 hours of work for cloth and 80 for wine. England needs 100 and 120.
But England is relatively better at cloth than wine, while Portugal is relatively better at wine than cloth.
So England puts its 220 hours into cloth, 2.2 units. Portugal puts its 170 hours into wine, 2.125 units. Without specialising, those hours made just one unit of each.
Total output of both goods rises, and swapping cloth for wine can leave both countries with more. That is comparative advantage.

probes.question: In the story, what happens to total production when each country focuses on its comparative advantage?
True or false: in the story, Portugal needs fewer hours than England for both cloth and wine.
